rationale: dual_domain_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=3, pretrain_steps=0, n_iter=50, grad_clip=1.0, outer_wall_s=1400, per_scene_s=None, batch_size=1, lr=0.0003, optimizer=adam, unet_c=16, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=iter-6 SIX-BOX. (1) PRIOR: iter-5 hr=0.0, lr 1e-3->3e-4 gave rmse=0.00633 (best yet, but still >> baseline 0.00521), ssim=0.941, 197/200. Gentler steps nudged rmse down ~1% -- not near baseline. Iters 1-5 (budget, per-scene fit, capacity, warm-start, lr) all pinned at hr=0. (2) FAILURE MODE: N2I converges toward the over-smoothed FBP-consistent mean; the self-supervision target caps recon RMSE above the sparse-FBP baseline. A known N2I pathology on dense phantoms is that MORE inner steps over-smooth MORE (the denoiser regresses to the low-frequency mean). (3) ONE KNOB: n_iter 200 -> 50 (early-stop; keep lr=3e-4, c=16, warm_start=True -- identical to iter-5 except inner-step count). (4) HYPOTHESIS: stopping the per-image fit early (50 steps) may HALT before the denoiser collapses to the over-smoothed mean, preserving more high-frequency detail from the warm-started init and LOWERING rmse toward baseline. If hr rises, over-smoothing is a late-optimization effect and early-stop is the lever. Per the documented ceiling, more likely the warm-started init is ALREADY over-smoothed so early-stop just freezes a still-blurry recon (hr=0). (5) BUDGET: 50 inner steps/scene is far under the 7.0s per-scene wall, so all 200 scans finish FAST (~3-4s each) -> loop well under 1400s; warm-start ep=3 + fast loop + figure ~= 12-15 min << 30-min wall. (6) Loop continues; iter-7 self-dispatched. Reserved levers: lr up (3e-3), pretrain_epochs up (10), unet_c=8, grad_clip, n_iter mid (100).
